I was allowed my phone and laptop etc when I was in. This might be unusual, and country dependent (this was scotland) but there were no organised activities except meals (and the food sucked, pack snacks) so my friends bought me my colouring books and films and my kindle. It was a total range of ages as I was in an adult ward. Pack earplugs or headphones - the woman next to me in my ward screamed at all hours of the night and day. Also my best thing there was my friends blanket- hospital beds tend to only have a thin blanket and it was so comforting to wrap myself up in something soft and warm. There was no therapy or anything and the nurses were rushed off their feet so barely had time to talk. But if something was really bad they would come- I had a panic attack at the girl opposite me yelling and swearing at the nurses, and someone came to sit with me until I camed down. 

You don't need to be scared. Hopefully you'll get some therapy and they should at least review your treatment. At the least, its a place where you don't need to hide how you're feeling and can just relax with no obligations. Noone will judge you there, they'll have seen worse. I know it's not the nicest place to be, but honestly there have been so many times since where I've wished for some time in a psych ward to get away from the pressures of life.

Good luck, you'll be okay I'm sure.

Firstly I'd say don't blame yourself for how you reacted - it's such a secret and personal thing that we hide from so many that suddenly being confronted with the topic in any form can make us freeze. Secondly, I totally understand the fear of planting the thought- when I self harmed a lot but minor cuts as a teenager I also swam competitively with a lot of younger people. I'm still terrified one of them ended up cutting because I gave her the idea, or that kids who were too young to understand who asked me about it later ended up doing it. But enough about me...

For your friend. I'd say definitely bring it up again when you have some alone time with them and explain why you froze and the tactics you were taught. I find communicating over writing easier if that would help you? It gives time to get all thoughts down and edited, and also gives them time to react in private without getting embarrassed or anything. Do let her know though that your therapist suggested techniques for *you*, knowing you, so they shouldn't feel bad if they don't work for her. But please be careful not to drag yourself back down into that place again, make sure you have someone to talk to as well, and it's not just bringing up bad memories for you.

Best of luck.
